title: Speed-Feed x PSN Wiring — compose all value-add system-viz nodes into the SF calculation engines and decisioning pipeline
brief: The /forge-audit-v2 SF x PSN value-node audit (2026-05-22) measured a 96.6% algorithm-module composition gap (2 of 59 src/algorithms/ modules composed by the 17 SF engines), 3 of 6 PSN surfaces unconnected (obsidian-brain/memory, wiki, system-viz), and a doc/reality drift regression (false Loewen-Shaw + stability-lobe header claims). This milestone wires the value-add nodes into the Speed-Feed calculation pipeline so PSN (Obsidian brain + PRISM OS + neural/AI ladder + wiki + tribal) and the AI systems are properly utilized for the most accurate AND cost-efficient cutting parameters. Each unit is domain-tagged speedfeed -> routes to slot juliett. Each unit declares its own re-measurement channel via scripts/sf-psn-leverage-rank.mjs.

decomposition_history.reason: Mid-iter discovery: KienzleForceModel and ExtendedTaylorModel are NOT semantic equivalents of the engine's inline kienzleCuttingForce()/extendedTaylorToolLife(). Kienzle: module's rake reference is 6° (vs inline 0°) and module applies an edge-radius correction (inline has none) — feasible to shim via edge_radius_mm=0.001 + rake_angle_deg+6. Taylor: STRUCTURAL formula mismatch — inline is canonical T=(C/(V·f^m·d^p))^(1/n) with m=p=0.1, module's docstring states T=(C·k_corr)/(V^(1/n)·f^a·ap^b) with ISO-group-specific a∈[0.6,0.85] and b∈[0.3,0.42]. No bit-equivalent shim exists; need formula reconciliation. Detail in knowledge/memories/reference/reference_sf_psn_u02_semantic_gap_2026_05_22.md.

units.closedReason: ExtendedTaylorModel.calculate() gained inline_compat?: boolean flag on TaylorInput. When true, calculate() short-circuits validation + corrections and emits T=(C/(V*f^0.1*d^0.1))^(1/n) clamped [1,600] — bit-equivalent to engine's pre-shim extendedTaylorToolLife(). UltimateSpeedFeedEngine.extendedTaylorToolLife() (line 972) delegates to the module for default m=p=0.1; non-default m/p falls through to local copy. Composed algorithm modules: 3 → 4 of 59. TaylorShimEquivalence.test.ts (13 cases, 480 fixtures, REL_TOLERANCE 1e-10) anti-regresses the swept shim. Spec §1 revised per the §7 approval gate after reading the module's calculate() body — docstring was wrong on (a) C placement inside ^(1/n) and (b) reference-value normalization of f/ap; spec's 'orders-of-magnitude divergence' refuted (real ~5% for ISO-P/n=0.25). Pre-existing UltimateSpeedFeedEngine.test.ts pass-rate unchanged (52 tests, 6 pre-existing failures — same 6 as U-02A baseline). Typecheck clean on 3 modified files. THREE peer-sweep misattributions this /loop session (c1b6428a62 in iter3 + this double-sweep) — recurring shared-tree hazard documented in [[reference_sf_psn_peer_sweep_recurrence_2026_05_22]].
units.description: ExtendedTaylorModel cannot be shimmed bit-equivalent to the engine's inline extendedTaylorToolLife() (UltimateSpeedFeedEngine.ts:925) — the formulas are structurally different. Inline: T = (C / (V * f^m * d^p))^(1/n) with m=p=0.1 (canonical extended-Taylor, single ^(1/n) over the C/X ratio). Module per its docstring: T = (C * k_coat * k_temp * k_hard) / (V^(1/n) * f^a * ap^b) with a∈[0.6,0.85], b∈[0.3,0.42] per ISO group (corrections multiply C as a NUMERATOR rather than X as a denominator, and the exponent topology differs). For ISO P with V=150, C=250, f=0.15, d=2: inline emits ~12 min; the module's docstring formula emits ~1.8e-6 min — orders-of-magnitude divergence that suggests the docstring under-specifies the actual implementation. This unit (1) reads ExtendedTaylorModel.calculate() body to confirm the actual formula, (2) decides between (a) extending the module with an `inline_compat` mode that reproduces the engine's m=p=0.1 form, or (b) accepting the module's more-accurate extended form and updating downstream test fixtures. Both paths require a written design decision + 3-of-3 review.
units.verifies_via: spec emitted at state/shared/specs/SF-PSN-TAYLOR-FORMULA-RECONCILIATION-2026-05-XX.md with the decided path; if (a) shim passes its 50+ fixture equivalence test; if (b) anti-regression suite re-baselined and all SF tests re-passed
exit_conditions: Formula reconciliation spec shipped + 3-of-3 approved
Either ExtendedTaylorModel composed via shim (option a) OR engine lifted to module-native with re-baselined tests (option b)
All SF tests green
Typecheck clean
